content.label: Bear is fantastic; it’s clean, pretty, and has all the features it needs, but on mobile, it’s very laggy when typing or scrolling. Definitely not a me problem, but a Bear problem. It hurts the experience quite a bit.

This app while feature rich is clutter free!
Making note taking and organizing fun again!!
I would be alright if these companies just sold the product and not the subscription. I do not want to pay for the same product 5 times over.
Love this app. It has a really clean and snappy interface. The only thing I would like to see is the ability to add a password to the app that isn’t tied to your system password/FaceID.

Ideas,songs,quotes,paint colors…room for everything without being a space hog. So many things to remember, and still be able to find. Bear is my stone to remember, and my rock to jump from. 
Merci, Maggie

Bear is great!  Two small requests, tho:
a) The ability to have bi-directional links would be a huge plus;
b) Graphic representation of how notes are connected.

Any chance of this in the future?  It would push my rating to 5 stars!

I don’t write app reviews. Ever. Call it laziness or not thinking it makes a difference or any number of things that say more about me than the apps. But Bear is different. I didn’t just download it recently. I’ve had it installed for years. I’ve gone through periods where I needed to sync between my iPhone and my Mac and I happily paid the $1.49 that month to get my documents migrated over. For a note-taking app, project planner, jotting down lyrics to a song that I want to look up later, adding things to a grocery list, or writing an outline to a story, I always turn to Bear. This morning, I figured it was time to write a review.

Bear has everything you need and nothing that you don’t. It just… works. Honestly, having the ability to sync everything across multiple devices for $14.99 a year is a ridiculously good deal. I’m not sure why I paid monthly when I’ve needed that functionality instead of just dropping the $15 for the whole year. I’ve spent more than that renting bad movies and I’ll never get that time back. In short (that ship has sailed), just download and try it. 99% of the features are free anyway so you’ve got nothing to lose. But I have a feeling it will be a go-to app for you like it is for me. So much so that you almost forget it’s not an integrated first party app.

I have only just purchased an install this, but it seems to be a great app. I love the fact that I can dictate into my watch and it will pop up on my phone and I open the app on my phone later on. It is very easy for me an older blue-collar worker to use. I’m sure there will be. Best used cases for me to discover, but for now being able to dictate to my watch on a job site is absolutely huge. I couldn’t be happier. -day 2 OMG! Minimalistic yet somehow includes everything practical!-
I love the way they create lists or to do lists. So good I deleted Apple “Notes”

title.label: No updates now for the last year

content.label: I’d be inclined to give a 5 star review if the software received regular updates… still a quality app but it could be so much more with regular updates and new features/functionalities. The app had great momentum for a while a few years ago and they have lost that due to what I perceive (assume, I suppose) to be a lackluster effort. I apologize if I am mistaken in my assumption.
Trying out premium and does not sync between devices. Bummer.

title.label: Cool app but lacks family sharing.

content.label: This app is very well designed and functions nicely. But…we have too many people in our family to buy multiple subscriptions. It’s one of the few apps of its kind that doesn’t have family in app purchase sharing.

This app is so CLEAN. I love taking notes with Bear- it’s clutter-free, has beautiful themes and it is so intuitive. I love the way tags work! As a dev myself, it’s so nice to be able to tag code snippets in multiple places so I can review them later. Great work!! 😄

I really like the tagging feature for organizing. Allows for creative structures and understands that a note doesn’t necessarily belong to single folder.
I think this is perfect for research and learning based notes, but also works for personal stuff.

This app is phenomenal, I often look at as the Discord of Note taking. However, a lot of the small features I am truly excited for are within the Beta, and I'm very anxious to get to use those on my iPad.

I did not like this app when it first came out, but it grew on me and used it extensively recently. As noted by others, the app has not been updated in months which is not necessarily a bad thing for a good app, but not good for a subscription based app that did not change anything after iOS 16 came out. The developer website indicated Bear 2.0 was coming soon, but that was a year ago. The developer has not replied to any reviews in a long time, while keeps posting on social media. I have transferred all my entries in Bear to other apps, and deleted it the app from my Macs, iPhone and iPad. It is really a shame.

title.label: Nice app but no support outside Apple ecosystem..

content.label: I have been using this app for a while and I love this app, but the lack of support on browser or on Android is frustrating.. I have been waiting for the web browser support for almost two years now because it was posted on bear website. After two years wait I'm finally moving to a different platform that supports a wider ecosystem.

title.label: Two years and still going strong!

content.label:
I left Evernote two years ago and spent several weeks transferring all my Evernote files to Bear. Very happy with the switch and I use it just about every day. 

No glitches or problems and all for $15 per year. 

I do hope the Panda update will become a reality one of these days but have not heard or seen anything in many months about that. Hope 2023 will bring that into full use. 

Thanks for a great app!

Robert Purdum

title.label: Just too unreliable to inspire confidence

content.label:
Finally giving up on Bear.
It’s nicely designed but the syncing between devices is horribly buggy and inconsistent.
I’ve ended up with so many versions of different docs and I never feel safe that everything is properly saved.
Back to Google docs while looking for an alternative.

title.label: The ultimate notes app for power users

content.label:
I cannot rate this high enough. I have been using bear for years and also am using their Pro version.

Markdown support (formatting text rapidly with easy to use code syntax) is a game changer (and my biggest factor in choosing a notes app) and their tagging system is genius. This app is so powerful and I use it every day for everything. I looked through tons of notes apps before I found this one. I cannot imagine life without it. It has everything I need and is gorgeous and snappy at the same time.
Dear Developer, When are you releasing Panda ? I think I’ve waited too long. Please reply… Yours truly, A frustrated Bear fan about to switch to Apple Notes.

title.label: If you’re not sure about this app…

content.label: It’s seriously worth your time to try. Explore and see if you can shape this up into what you’re looking for. Thanks for an inspiring experience, Shiny Frog team.

I used bear to write my first Poetry Book, The Shades of Us. There’s something about opening this app that makes me feel motivated. I’ve tried other ones that have great features, but its just not the same. Definitely worth a try if you’re still looking and haven’t found the right program for you!

I don’t know I opened the app once I downloaded it and installed it and there’s really nothing there.  Reminds me of working with DOS or something there’s no user interface at all.   Am I missing something here?  Evernote was so much easier and more straightforward and colorful.  Evernote  actually has a user interface, so I guess I’m gonna stick with that.   What’s missing?  Couldn’t find an option to even leave a voice recording which they stated you can do.  Where is the microphone?   Sorry but I was not able to find it so that means your user interface stinks.  Do I have to pay a fee for the microphone?  Hmmm. Confusion about this App only means one thing. You uninstall it and get rid of it.  Evernote RULES!!

It’s fast, accurate, formatted properly and if I could think of more ultra positive words I’d add them. 
Notes are simple to find. 
Bear never gets in the way of my workflow in any way. 
I’d recommend this app to anyone.

This is a really nice writing app.. Better than most in fact (on the Mac as well). Subscription is pricey but I guess it’s worth it since I pay it lol.  iCloud sync is great and everything is fast. Get it !
Very good app but please add option to search text within notes

title.label: It was great… at one point.

content.label:
This app was top-of-the-line (and could be compared) to the likes of Evernote, back when this app originally released. Back when the competitive market all had less features. But after 4-5 years, it seems Bear still hasn’t added any new features that matter to the user. It also seems likes they only respond to 5-star reviews, so overall just not a great look and really makes you feel like the developers gave up on the app and are just now milking it. 

I truly wish they would have added more support for it. I loved the elegancy, the aesthetic, and just how great it felt to use. I even use Avenir Next for almost all fonts that I can change haha, but the sudden halt in innovation for the app is what ultimately helped me move on from it. Haven’t touched this app (properly) in a long time. 

Hopefully they realize they may still have a chance here before their, soon, demise.
It works pretty well i like the nesting features. I use this for formatting and simple note for just plain text notes. Great combo

I am loving this app. The only issue I have is that the watch new note button is taking me to a keyboard and I have to click on the microphone there. Does anyone know how to fix this? I am getting the pro version because I am really liking this, and it is making note taking so much easier.

Beautiful design. I really wanted to use it to host my slip-box, but I noticed that the various crisscrossing links in my notes cascaded changes across multiple notes causing them to link to other notes than originally specified.
Of all of the text editors I’ve been experimenting with, drafts is by far the most comfortable, with a robust library and community for support and learning. I love it!

I havent had a mac for awhile, but Bear notes has always been my favorite note taking app, Ive tried everything else and I have now returned. I paid for the yearly, reloaded up the app and to my amazement notes I wrote 4 and 5 years ago were still saved. I wasnt expecting that at all and it just blew me away. WOW!

The UI and UX of this app is superior to anything else Ive used in my life. It really is best in class and for the cost of one to two trips to starbucks you can have this app for an entire year! It helps me blog, study, be creative, its my go to digital note taking app for all sorts of things. 

I cannot thank the developers enough for somehow keeping my notes for this long, and I am sorry I left, and I am so happy to have returned. If there is any bear swag I can buy please let me know. Mugs, shirts, hats, I want to rep the brand and spread the word. 

A+, 5 stars, 11/10, best in class, for everyone from creatives to business minds, you must try this app for your note taking, your blog drafting, poem writing, script and books, journaling and tasks, recipes and more!

Bear definitely is special. The markdown support is awesome, even if your new to markdown it’s quick to pick up. 
I’m excited for the 2.0 changes especially tables! I’ve played around with Panda for a bit and think 2.0 will be even better. 

If you’re looking for a lightweight albeit powerful notes app, this is it. Also, at $15/yr it beats other apps by a lot.
Arabic?

title.label: After years of use, Bear is still excellent

content.label:
Over time, notepads become jumbled with excess information. Many apps solve this with complex softwares. Bear can bear the load of years of unrelated information without being complex. Intuitive sorting methods combine with succinct functionality to produce an app that is very simple. After years of use, I have no desire to move on from Bear.
(Also, my eyes thank you for dark mode).

title.label: By far my favorite replacement for Apple Notes

content.label: It’s quick and easy, yet sophisticated enough to handle some more advanced things. I look forward to the next iteration of the app, code named Panda?, when the team is finally able to finish it.
Please add tables - 5 stars for the memories but I will move on from bear as my notes hub if there’s isn’t a release soon
Use it very often and highly recommend.

I was writing on this, it’s pretty good overall, but I just noticed there is no backup option. For example, I was writing a speech in one of the notes, and I erased a whole paragraph of content by mistake. I can’t get back and recover that paragraph. (I’m not saying erase the complete document, I’m not saying that.) you can recover erased documents. I’m talking about the literal freedom of undoing mistakes, which you get when you mess up with something but can recover by simply pressing an option.

But maybe there is a backup option, but I haven’t found that option yet, which shouldn’t be so difficult to find.

Other than that, the app it’s pretty good.

title.label: Simplistic Interface with Intuitive Tagging System

content.label:
I have been using Bear for more or less three years now. This app has seen my two master’s degree and now on my way to my PhD. 

For someone with a short attention span and lack of organization, Bear is the app I use on a daily basis for note taking, manuscript editing, and brainstorming. I love that the user interface is minimalistic with barely any distractions. The fact that I can write in a markdown format allows me to essentially never have to leave the keyboard during writing. In addition substitution price is very reasonable. 

I will likely stick to Bear in the foreseeable future and hopefully see some light new features for those who are more pictorially oriented.

I have been trying to get a good notes/journal and logging my time/work/life/adventure system. I was done searching… I don’t like subscription model usage. I have been working all my notes through markdown and pushing the changes to GitHub with a weekly branch. Sounds easy, and it is, but there is a lot of messing with the git process real fiddley and sorta tuff to go back and fix. I got a good flow and it was working until I had a crazy week then a crazier week then a crazy week and I started thinking, why am I doing all this crazy stuff, just find an app that does mark down and you can just take notes. On my iPad (type, pencil, screen), on my MacBook, on my iPhone, these all work and this is only $1.50 a month. That’s way worth my time that I have been busting through the git process. I’m glad I found you and you aren’t crazy expensive.

Thanks,
I am rating this app 4 stars because I think that the passcode for privacy should come in the free version

title.label: Enjoying the app a lot save for one big annoyance

content.label: I love this app, the use of nested tags and linking while maintaining the lightweight feel of the app is wonderful. My one complaint that prevents me from giving it 5 starts is something that I’ve encountered dozens of times in my short time using this app on my ipad pro. When I open the app, the app opens to the last note I was working on. When I try to continue working on it, I have to leave the note entirely and go back into it otherwise it constantly makes the page jump down to blank space after all the text. And when I click my cursor where I want to continue typing, it continues jumping the page down, making it near impossible to continue using the note. So I have to leave the note and go back in to get it to stop. Sounds minor but extremely annoying when you’re working frequently within one note.
This app is amazing I love how the font isn’t to big and it’s very well organized I definitely prefer this over any other app especially apple note taking!!!!! :))))))
The app is frictionless and snappy, no lag, no loading times, just reliable and smooth in every aspect. It’s also the best value of any note app i have come across.

This company does not prioritize customer needs and is very very slow to add many mass requested features. The page of development and improvements are absolutely glacial. I would not recommend entrusting your notes to this product as you will be left disappointed in the end.

title.label: no search within note, and the staff seems to think that's okay

content.label:
there's no "pipeline" because doing so is not something they want to do. there's other things "more important" than adding an incredibly basic search function inside a note, like finishing a web app. reading the response of the staff on the subreddit and getting a sense of how the company thinks of its users' requests was eye-opening, to say the least.

i tried it. it's a nice little app with a nice design. just be aware what you're paying for.
It works and has basic options, but if you need something cross platform like me (PC, Mac, iPhone, iPad) then you should look at Obsidian.  Bear hasn't added any meaningful features in years.

I'm a scattered brained human by nature, plus I'm homeschooling our 5 kids (aged between 14-4) and I am also in college, so there's a lot of info I need to scribble down on the fly or things that I've got to remind to get done & a lot of times before this app-- nothing got done! This app has saved me hours of headaches & I even feel good about myself not wasting so much paper writing one or two little things down, only to lose it. It took me a second to fall in love with Bear, but that's my own stubborn anti-technologies mindset. This app is quite literally like having a personal assistant//babysitter for myself!!!!
